statement: Chinese demand for Nvidia H200 is very large but only trivially fulfilled under export licensing: ~10 Chinese firms (Alibaba, Tencent, ByteDance, JD.com) are cleared to buy up to 75,000 chips each and ~$10 billion of H200 licenses are approved, yet actual shipments remain 'trivial'; Chinese firms had ordered over 2 million H200 for 2026 against ~700,000 units of Nvidia inventory, and Blackwell remains banned.
why: Case-by-case licensing has begun to reopen a China channel for H200-class chips amid enormous latent Chinese demand, but a 25% tariff, volume caps, limited inventory and a continued Blackwell ban keep realized shipments minimal.

impact.mechanism: A reopened but tightly capped China licensing regime unlocks only a sliver of a very large latent demand pool for Nvidia H200s, so the addressable-demand upside is real but heavily constrained.

evidence.excerpt: For the American people, the bottom line is very few shipments against licenses for H200s and equivalents have taken place

confidence.basis: Congressional testimony relayed by a single secondary outlet (mlq.ai citing CNBC/Bloomberg/Reuters); no primary transcript fetched.

dispersion: conflicting same-key reports: statement/trend changed (trend rising -> rising); sources: Investing.com, MLQ News (mlq.ai)
